clue.text: Reportedly cut down beam, revealing moonstone, perhaps?

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the phrase that follows is heard rather than read

parts.note: a beam that has been cut down is a felled spar

explanation.surface: A lumberjack fells a beam and finds a gemstone inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, FELLED SPAR runs together into the mineral's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonstone is one variety of this mineral group, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Toiling away at first developing engraved design

indicators.note: developing suggests change and growth, so the letters before it are worked into a new form
at first points to the opening letter of the word away

explanation.surface: Someone toiling away at the start of a project develops a carved pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes A from 'away'; 'developing' rearranges TOILING plus that A.
explanation.definitionFit: An intaglio is a design cut into a surface, the opposite of a cameo, so an engraved design.

clue.text: Exactly like Edgar Wallace's four men!

definitions.meaning: exactly in the sense of precisely
Edgar Wallace wrote the thriller The Four ... Men, about righteous vigilantes

explanation.walkthrough: Edgar Wallace was a popular British thriller writer of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means precisely as an adverb and fair or righteous as an adjective, the title's sense.

clue.text: Sprawling on Alice's huge couch

indicators.note: sprawling suggests limbs spread every which way, so the following letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: the word with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Alice lounges about on her enormous sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: A long upholstered seat with a backrest at one end is a type of couch.

clue.text: Sheets of low cloud indispensable to most ratings

indicators.note: something indispensable to a phrase is part of its very fabric, so the letters lie inside most ratings

explanation.surface: Low cloud is said to be essential to the best television audience figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus clouds form flat low sheets; the plural of stratus is used here.

clue.text: What some do in jail, finally feel heartache

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word jail

parts.note: to anguish is to feel deep distress

explanation.surface: Prisoners end up suffering emotional pain in their cells.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description: what prisoners do in jail is pine away.
explanation.definitionFit: People are said to waste away or pine in prison, the idiom of being left to rot in a cell.

clue.text: Good bloke that is a constructor of courses?

parts.note: a brick is old slang for a reliable, good-hearted person
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A decent chap turns out to be someone who builds racecourses or golf courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' are not racing or meals but the horizontal layers of bricks in a wall; a brickie is British slang for a bricklayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bricklayer builds a wall up in layers of bricks, each layer called a course.

clue.text: Who made a bit investing gold in marine transport

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so the ship wraps around the metal

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Someone who put a little money into a cruise ship by investing gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' is the metal mouthpiece of a horse's bridle, not a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A loriner is a craftsman making bits, spurs and other metal parts of horse harness.

clue.text: Stood up to sibling endlessly in debt?

indicators.note: in places the shortened relative inside the word for debt

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of sister is dropped

parts.note: a sister is a female sibling

explanation.surface: Someone refused to let a brother or sister fall permanently into debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in the red' is the banking idiom for owing money, which is why debt gives the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist someone is to stand up to them or oppose them.

clue.text: Time to devise material for roof

parts.note: to hatch a plan is to devise it

explanation.surface: It's time to come up with something to cover the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reeds laid on a roof form a traditional covering material.

clue.text: Rebuttal of accusation from one tucking into seafood at bar?

parts.note: a counter is a bar where drinks or food are served

indicators.note: tucking into means pushing inside, so the numeral goes inside the shellfish

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish eaten as seafood
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone eating shellfish at a bar fights back against an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating but puts I inside CLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim made in response to an accusation or claim against oneself serves as a rebuttal.

clue.text: From Scottish island making north western US state

indicators.note: making signals that one letter becomes another, north turning into western

parts.note: Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Someone moves from a Scottish island to the northwest of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is a midwestern state of the USA.

clue.text: Good publicity surrounding idle pleasure-seeker

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
about means around or surrounding

explanation.surface: Positive press coverage gathers around a lazy hedonist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flits from one amusement to another is a restless seeker of pleasure.

clue.text: A blow possibly involving plant in Cambs city

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the city wraps around the flower

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, abbreviated Cambs
an aster is a daisy-like garden plant

explanation.surface: A flower in an English cathedral city takes a knock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' is a wind, not a strike; Ely is a small cathedral city near Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind from the east is named after its direction, and a wind is something that blows.

clue.text: One who will mimic flightless bird audibly by and by

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the bird and the later time run together when spoken

parts.note: by and by means later on

explanation.surface: A mimic will imitate the sound of an emu eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second half is a sound-alike: the word for 'by and by' is respelt to fit after the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who copies or tries to equal another is an imitator, one who mimics.

clue.text: Londoner's wife gets suit, going round high-class sale

parts.note: in Cockney slang 'my old Dutch' means my wife

indicators.note: going round means the lawsuit wraps around the letter for upper class

parts.note: a suit in law is an action
U is the abbreviation for upper-class

explanation.surface: A Cockney's wife buys a suit at a smart auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my old Dutch' is East London (Cockney) slang for one's wife. 'suit' is a lawsuit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch auction is a sale where the price starts high and drops until someone bids.

clue.text: Italian bread broken by a key violinist once

indicators.note: broken by means the bread is split open with other letters inserted

parts.note: panini are Italian bread rolls
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: An Italian sandwich interrupted by a piano key and a famous fiddler.
explanation.walkthrough: AG goes in after the P of PANINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was a celebrated nineteenth-century Italian virtuoso of the violin.

clue.text: Savoury dish made by one's son, in part

indicators.note: in places the letters for one's son inside the word for part

parts.note: a role is a part in a play
I is one, so one's is I'S, written IS

explanation.surface: A dish prepared partly by somebody's son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part' looks like 'partly' but means inside ROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried cake of minced meat or fish coated in breadcrumbs is a savoury dish.

clue.text: Hot German bread one left to be cut

indicators.note: to be cut means removed, so one letter is taken out

parts.note: stollen is a German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas
L is the abbreviation for left, one of the two in the bread

explanation.surface: Hot German bread with a slice to be taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' is slang for stolen goods, not temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for goods that have been taken illegally.

clue.text: Advertisement showing dog crossing lake

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the dog breed wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A commercial shows a dog crossing a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is informal for a piece of promotional publicity, a brief puff for a product.

clue.text: Jointly travel to north secured by rope, perhaps

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the rope, which wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a tether is a rope used to tie an animal, and rope is one example

indicators.note: to north in a down clue means read upwards, so the word is turned around

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Two people set off northward roped together for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'to north' means upward, so the word is reversed as the grid reads top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something together means doing it jointly, in combination.

clue.text: It takes one an hour to make a knot

definitions.text: It takes one an hour to make a knot

parts.words: It takes one an hour to make a knot
parts.note: reads like slow fingers tying a rope, but a knot is a ship's speed: one unit of sea distance covered per hour

explanation.surface: Someone takes a whole hour to tie a single knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a speed of one sea distance unit, about 1,852 metres, per hour.

clue.text: Where flighty types may go for a walk in SW London?

definitions.meaning: flighty types are birds, which are kept in a cage

definitions.text: for a walk in SW London?
definitions.meaning: ... Walk is a street by St James's Park in Westminster, south-west London

explanation.walkthrough: Birdcage Walk runs along St James's Park near Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds are put in a wire enclosure, and the London street name supplies the second sense.

clue.text: Not in fashion, Society's acts of wanton violence

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
the rage is the current fashion
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Being unfashionable is society's form of brutal crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrages are shocking acts of cruelty or violence.

clue.text: Deliberate avoidance upset Welsh ace

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Welsh champion is upset by being deliberately ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is to shun on purpose; the noun form means deliberately avoiding something.

clue.text: Teach Europeans about former Continental currency

indicators.note: about means around, so the two letters for Europeans wrap the coin

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, doubled for the plural
the ducat was a gold coin once used across Europe

explanation.surface: Teaching Europeans about the old coins of the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: To educate someone is to teach or instruct them.

clue.text: Male vicar possibly accepted by 50% of politicians?

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so the clergyman goes inside the half word
50% of keeps half the word, its first three letters

parts.note: Tories are UK Conservative politicians
Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar, among other clergy

explanation.surface: A male vicar may be welcomed by half the politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR, half of TORIES, takes in REV.
explanation.definitionFit: Trevor is a male first name, so the definition indicates a man's name by example.

clue.text: Ruin a Continental celebration

parts.note: un is French for a
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A European party is spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo something is to ruin or bring it to nothing.
